description: National SC/ST population anchor points from the two most recent Indian censuses, plus a total-population reference series used to compute SC/ST population SHARE by year (not just absolute counts). India has not held a census since 2011 (the 2021 census was postponed indefinitely). Used by scripts/common/population_projection.py.

total_population_by_year.note: UN World Population Prospects (2024 Revision), mid-year (July 1) estimates -- a DIFFERENT source/methodology from the Census 2011 total above (which was taken around March 2011, ~1.211 billion vs. UN's mid-2011 estimate of ~1.261 billion, a ~4% difference from differing reference dates and estimation methods). Used here only as the denominator for computing SC/ST population SHARE by year; SC/ST absolute population counts themselves still come from the Census-anchored CAGR projection, not from UN figures.
total_population_by_year.source: UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division, World Population Prospects: The 2024 Revision.

obc_general_note: No equivalent projection is possible for OBC or General population share. India's census has not enumerated caste beyond SC/ST since 1931 -- the commonly-cited OBC figures (~52% from the Mandal Commission, 1980, itself an extrapolation from the 1931 count; ~41% from NSSO 1999-2000/2006 sample surveys) are two different old estimates using different methods, not two points on a trend that can be projected forward the way SC/ST's 2001->2011 census figures can. 'General/Other' as a residual (100% - SC% - ST% - OBC%) inherits all of that uncertainty: using the NSSO figure implies ~34% General; using Mandal's implies ~23% -- an 11-point swing depending purely on which decades-old OBC estimate is chosen. This is why population-share benchmarks elsewhere in this project are computed for SC/ST only, never for OBC/General.

obc_general_estimates.note: Two old, non-comparable, non-official guesses -- not a range with a 'true' value somewhere inside it, and not two points on a trend. Shown side by side, never averaged or blended into one number, so neither is misread as more authoritative than the other. SC/ST shares used for the residual are the exact 2011 Census figures (16.63% SC, 8.61% ST), not the UN-denominator-adjusted per-year projection used elsewhere -- this is a single point-in-time illustration, not part of the year-by-year series.

scenarios.label: Using the Mandal Commission's OBC estimate
scenarios.obc_source: Mandal Commission Report, 1980 (itself an extrapolation from the 1931 Census, the last to enumerate caste beyond SC/ST)

census_2001.publisher: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India

census_2011.publisher: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India

un_wpp.publisher: UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division

nsso.report: Employment and Unemployment Survey, NSS 55th Round (1999-2000) -- the source of the commonly-cited ~41% OBC estimate; the 61st Round (2004-05) covers the same ground
nsso.publisher: National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

mandal_commission.report: Report of the Backward Classes Commission ("Mandal Commission Report"), 1980
